title: Given a Scenario, Configure Microsoft Windows Settings

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Windows configuration is distributed across Control Panel, Settings, File Explorer, administrative tools, and device interfaces.
The main mental model is: task → correct Windows settings area.
sections.callout: Know the destination by its function, not only by the appearance of a particular Windows release.

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: When a Windows configuration scenario appears, can you identify which settings area controls it?
bullets: Network sharing → Network and Sharing Center

entries.title: Internet Options
paragraphs: Controls legacy browser and Internet properties such as security zones, connections, privacy, certificates, and proxy-related behavior.
entries.recognitionCue: Browser or legacy Internet properties → Internet Options.

entries.title: Devices and Printers
paragraphs: Provides user-facing access to printers and some connected peripherals.
entries.recognitionCue: Set a default printer → Devices and Printers.

entries.title: Program and Features
paragraphs: Programs and Features manages, modifies, or uninstalls traditional desktop applications.
entries.recognitionCue: Remove a classic Windows program → Programs and Features.

entries.title: Network and Sharing Center
paragraphs: Provides traditional network status, adapter, and sharing configuration.
entries.recognitionCue: Configure network sharing in Control Panel → Network and Sharing Center.

entries.title: System (Control Panel)
paragraphs: Shows computer-wide Windows and hardware information and links to advanced system options.

entries.title: Windows Defender Firewall
paragraphs: Controls firewall profiles, application allowances, and inbound or outbound rules.
entries.recognitionCue: Allow or block network traffic → Windows Defender Firewall.

entries.title: Mail
paragraphs: Manages profiles for supported desktop mail clients.
entries.recognitionCue: Configure a desktop mail profile → Mail.

entries.title: Sound
paragraphs: Configures playback and recording devices, speakers, microphones, and related behavior.

entries.title: User Accounts
paragraphs: Manages Control Panel user-account settings.

entries.title: Device Manager
paragraphs: Manages hardware, drivers, and device status.
entries.recognitionCue: Fix a driver or hardware device → Device Manager.

entries.title: Indexing Options
paragraphs: Controls locations and content included in Windows Search indexing.
entries.recognitionCue: A searchable folder is missing from results → Indexing Options.

entries.title: Administrative Tools
paragraphs: Provides shortcuts to advanced Windows management utilities.

sections.title: File Explorer Options
paragraphs: File Explorer Options controls general folder behavior and view settings.

entries.title: View Hidden Files
paragraphs: The View settings can display files and folders normally marked hidden.

entries.title: Hide Extensions
paragraphs: Windows can hide known file extensions. Technicians often show them to identify real file types, including deceptive names such as invoice.pdf.exe.

entries.title: General Options
paragraphs: General options change broad File Explorer behavior such as folder-opening preferences.

entries.title: View Options
paragraphs: View options determine how files and folders are displayed.

sections.title: Power Options

entries.title: Hibernate
paragraphs: Writes the session to storage and powers down, using less continuing power than sleep.

entries.title: Power Plans
paragraphs: A power plan defines performance, display, sleep timing, and energy-use behavior.

entries.title: Sleep/Suspend
paragraphs: Keeps the session in RAM in a low-power state for fast resume.

entries.title: Standby
paragraphs: Standby is another term associated with a low-power sleep state.

entries.title: Choose What Closing the Lid Does
paragraphs: A laptop can sleep, hibernate, shut down, or do nothing when its lid closes.

entries.title: Turn On Fast Startup
paragraphs: Fast Startup uses a hybrid shutdown process to accelerate the next boot; it is not normal sleep.

entries.title: USB Selective Suspend
paragraphs: Reduces power to individual idle USB devices.
entries.recognitionCue: A USB device powers down because of energy savings → USB selective suspend.

sections.callout: Sleep keeps the session in RAM; hibernate writes it to disk.

entries.title: Ease of Access
paragraphs: Provides Narrator, Magnifier, contrast, and input assistance.

entries.title: Time and Language
paragraphs: Controls date, time zone, region, language, and keyboard or input language.

entries.title: Update and Security
paragraphs: Contains Windows Update, recovery, and security-related areas in supported Windows Settings layouts.

entries.title: Personalization
paragraphs: Controls backgrounds, themes, colors, and lock-screen appearance.

entries.title: Apps
paragraphs: Manages installed applications, defaults, and application-related settings.

entries.title: Privacy
paragraphs: Controls application access to location, camera, microphone, files, and other protected resources.

entries.title: System (Windows Settings)
paragraphs: Contains core device, display, notification, storage, power, and OS behavior settings.

entries.title: Devices
paragraphs: Manages connected peripherals and device-related options.

entries.title: Network and Internet
paragraphs: Configures Wi-Fi, Ethernet, VPN, proxy, and other connections.

entries.title: Gaming
paragraphs: Controls Windows gaming-related features.

entries.title: Accounts
paragraphs: Controls sign-in, Microsoft accounts, family or other users, and work or school accounts.

sections.title: Control Panel vs. Settings
paragraphs: Windows exposes overlapping configuration through traditional Control Panel and the modern Settings app. CompTIA may name either destination.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Remove classic program → Programs and Features
Network sharing → Network and Sharing Center

entries.title: Programs and Features vs. Apps
paragraphs: Programs and Features is the traditional Control Panel destination; Apps is the modern Settings destination.

entries.title: Devices and Printers vs. Device Manager
paragraphs: Devices and Printers is user-facing; Device Manager troubleshoots hardware and drivers.

entries.title: Network and Sharing Center vs. Network and Internet
paragraphs: The former is traditional Control Panel; the latter is modern Settings.

entries.title: Sleep vs. Hibernate
paragraphs: Sleep keeps the session in RAM; hibernate writes it to storage.

entries.title: Fast Startup vs. Sleep
paragraphs: Fast Startup speeds boot after shutdown; sleep preserves an active session in low-power RAM.
